tasks.short: Install new equipment and peripherals on site, install operating software and configure settings, test with the user, and record the installation.

steps.what: Repair technician installs new equipment and peripheral equipment on site
Repair technician installs operating software and configures settings by hand
Repair technician tests the installed equipment with the user
Repair technician writes serial numbers and installation details on the paper work order

tasks.design: Each machine model gets a standard configuration package (operating software, drivers, network and printer settings) that a deployment tool applies when the machine is connected, so settings are not typed one by one. The work order in the field service app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) takes the serial number by barcode scan and has a fixed installation checklist. Installing hardware and testing with the user stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Settings were entered by hand per machine and installations written on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Deployment tools apply standard configuration packages; field service apps scan serial numbers.
tasks.still_hard: Older machines and special peripherals need settings by hand.
tasks.human_edge: Fitting equipment into a cramped office without blocking anything.

reach.learn: Whether machines work on first use.

evidence.claim: FieldBuddy offers work orders that fill themselves in and checklists for technicians.
Deployment tools can apply standard configuration packages to new machines.

assumptions: Boundary: from the installation job to the installation recorded; billing is outside.
Input contract: a configuration package per model; fallback is setting by hand.
research_questions: Do repeat visits after installation fall?

incremental.description: Repair technician updates configuration packages for new models.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many older machines; high: standard models in large roll-outs.

tasks.short: Read counters and error logs at each machine, combine the records in a spreadsheet, analyse them to assess how each machine is working, and note findings in the service record.

steps.what: Repair technician reads counters and error logs at each machine
Repair technician combines equipment performance records in a spreadsheet
Repair technician analyzes the records to assess equipment functioning
Repair technician notes findings in the service record

tasks.design: Networked printers, copiers and cash machines report counters and error codes to a remote monitoring tool, which feeds the asset records in the field service app ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so the technician does not read them at each machine. A dashboard shows error rates and counters per machine over time. Findings are noted on the asset record with fixed fields. Assessing how each machine is working stays with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counters and logs were read at each machine and combined by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Networked machines report counters and errors; field service apps keep asset records.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing that a feed roller is wearing before the errors show it.
tasks.altitude: The technician reads trends instead of collecting counters.

reach.learn: Whether visits can follow machine condition.

evidence.claim: FieldBuddy includes asset management in its field service tool.
Networked office machines can report counters and error codes to remote monitoring tools.

assumptions: Boundary: from the service round to findings noted; repairs are outside.
Input contract: machines networked and allowed to report; fallback is reading on site.
Customers allow machine data to leave their network.
s4 is the technician's first record of the findings and keeps its full time; transferring records to the service history is cut in sibling task 11631.

incremental.description: Repair technician checks machines that stop reporting.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many older machines; high: mostly networked fleets.

tasks.short: Diagnose the malfunction at the machine, look up fixes, reinstall software or adjust settings, and record the fix.

steps.what: Repair technician diagnoses machine malfunctions at the machine
Repair technician looks up fixes in manuals and vendor sites
Repair technician reinstalls software programs or adjusts settings at the machine
Repair technician records the fix on the paper work order

tasks.design: Past fixes are stored on the asset records in the field service app ({OTHER}) with fault code, cause and action, so the technician searches by model and fault code instead of manuals. Where the machine is networked, the remote management tool reinstalls the software package or pushes corrected settings, so the technician does not do it step by step at the machine. The fix is recorded with fixed fields on the work order. Diagnosing stays with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fixes were looked up in manuals and software reinstalled by hand at each machine.
tasks.enabler_now: Field service apps hold fix histories; remote tools reinstall software.
tasks.still_hard: Faults on older machines need hands-on work.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a fault that looks like software but is a loose cable.

reach.learn: Whether fault codes in reports are useful.

evidence.claim: FieldBuddy offers work orders with checklists and asset management for technicians.
Remote management tools can reinstall software and push settings to networked machines.

assumptions: Boundary: from the fault report to the fix recorded; part replacement is outside.
Input contract: fix history built up over time; fallback is manuals.
s4 is the first record of the fix and keeps its full time; transferring it to the service history is cut in sibling task 11631.
research_questions: Do repeat calls for the same fault fall?

incremental.description: Repair technician writes clear fix records for the history.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older machines; high: networked machines with known faults.

tasks.short: Write the work order with hours and parts, check it with the customer's signature, send it to the office, complete the repair bill, fill in time cards, and complete expense reports.

steps.what: Repair technician writes the work order with hours and parts on paper
Repair technician checks the final work order and gets the customer's signature
Repair technician photographs and e-mails the work order to the office
Repair technician completes repair bills from the work order
Repair technician fills in time cards in a spreadsheet
Repair technician completes expense reports with paper receipts

tasks.design: The work order lives in the field service app ({OPS_SYSTEM}): hours come from start and stop taps on the job, parts are scanned, and the serial number is taken from the asset. Once the technician has checked it and the customer has signed on the screen, it syncs to the office instead of being photographed and e-mailed. The repair bill is generated from the work order with the contract rates for the office's billing run ({ERP}), and work order hours fill the time card ({HCM}). Receipts are photographed into the expense app ({EXPENSE}), which reads date and amount.
tasks.previous_blocker: Work orders were written on paper, photographed, mailed and retyped; hours and expenses were entered again.
tasks.enabler_now: Field service apps turn work orders into bills and time records.
tasks.still_hard: Jobs without signal need the app to sync later.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining a bill to a customer who expected the repair to be covered.
tasks.altitude: The technician checks records instead of writing them several times.

reach.learn: Whether bills arrive complete and sooner.

evidence.claim: FieldBuddy fills work orders in, gives technicians checklists and converts a work order into an invoice automatically.
easyJet reported 80% less paper and paperwork processing cut by about 80% after adding e-signature to its maintenance system; self-reported by the airline.
Workflow systems and GPS in vans count as staff tracking systems that need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the job done to the expense report; sending invoices is outside.
Input contract: app linked to billing and time records; fallback is paper.
The technician checks every work order before it syncs.
Works council consent and a DPIA come before rollout.
research_questions: How soon after the job is the bill ready?

incremental.description: Repair technician corrects work orders the app checks reject.
